# RTP_Constraints_Course

A **teaching workspace**, not a code project. It runs on Matt Pocock's `teach` skill
(mattpocock-skills 1.2.3).

**Learner:** Joe Smith, assistant athletic trainer, Baylor Athletics.
**Sponsor:** Eric Rash.
**Topic:** ecological dynamics and the constraints-led approach (CLA) applied to the last
phase of return to performance in American football.

## How to work here

Type `/teach` in this directory. Do not hand-roll lessons — the skill owns the workflow.
`teach` and `ask-matt` are `disable-model-invocation: true`, so **a human must type the
slash command**; the agent cannot invoke them.

Read before doing anything: `MISSION.md`, then `NOTES.md` (open questions and framing
wrinkles), then `RESOURCES.md`.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MISSION.md` | Why Joe is learning this. Grounds every teaching decision. |
| `INTERVIEW.md` | **Mission interview to run with Joe. Do this before lesson 0001.** 45 min; Parts 1 and 2 are the ones that matter. |
| `RESOURCES.md` | Curated trusted sources. Most are already in Eric's SecondBrain library. |
| `NOTES.md` | Open questions, preferences, working notes. |
| `assets/` | Reusable lesson components. `course.css` is shared by every lesson. |
| `lessons/` | `NNNN-slug.html` — the unit of teaching. None written yet. |
| `reference/` | `*.html` cheat sheets. The compressed residue of lessons. |
| `docs/handoffs/` | Durable cross-session handoffs. Newest first. |
| `learning-records/` | `NNNN-slug.md` ADR-style records. Created lazily at the first record. |

## Rules specific to this workspace

- **Ground in `RESOURCES.md`, never in parametric knowledge.** This field has a lot of
  confident bad writing in it. Cite everything.
- **Football examples only.** Generic team-sport examples will not land with position coaches.
- **Every lesson ends in something Joe could do at practice tomorrow.**
- `GLOSSARY.md` does not exist yet by design — see `NOTES.md`.
- **Phase 2 is a drill-design tool.** Do not start it until the lessons have specified it.
  Route: `/grill-with-docs` → `/prototype` → `/implement`. Local-only per Baylor IT.

## Source library

Papers referenced as `LIB/…` live in `~/SecondBrain/Knowledge/library/research-papers/`.
Search with `memsearch search "<query>" --top-k 5`. Zotero MCP was down on 2026-09-01.

=== RESOURCES.md Gray book mentions ===
13:- **Rob Gray** — Professor, Arizona State University. Host of the [Perception & Action Podcast](https://perceptionaction.com/). Author of *How We Learn to Move*, *Learning to Optimize Movement*, and *Learning To Be an "Ecological" Coach* (**title corrected 2026-09-02 — this file previously said "How to Be an Ecological Coach"**). Read in that order; see the perceptionaction.com section below. The most accessible on-ramp for a clinician.
28:- **Yearby, T., Myszka, S., Roberts, W. M., Woods, C. T., & Davids, K. (2024).** Applying an ecological approach to practice design in American football: Some case examples on best practice. *Sports Coaching Review, 13*(3), 362–385. [doi:10.1080/21640629.2022.2057698](https://doi.org/10.1080/21640629.2022.2057698) · `key=7M8YQMKU`
36:- **Rob Gray — *How We Learn to Move: A Revolution in the Way We Coach & Practice Sports Skills*** (2021). **NOT YET IN THE LIBRARY — acquire.**
206:**Also worth reading, not rehab:** **["5 Principles for Effective Ecological Coaching"](https://emergentmvmt.com/5-principles-for-effective-ecological-coaching/)** by **Tyler Yearby** — a course pillar writing the framework in plain language, free. Performer–environment reciprocity · alive movement problems · constraining to afford · repetition without repetition · movement ownership. **Better first reading for Joe than any journal paper in this file, and it is by the lead author of the anchor paper.** Note principle 5's caveat: intervene when a pattern is **non-functional or injury-prone** — the clearest statement of where their approach concedes ground to a clinician.
232:| [Comparative Training Studies](https://perceptionaction.com/comparative/) | **Traditional vs ecological coaching, head to head.** This is the page Joe brings to a skeptical physician or position coach. **Probably the single most useful link in this file for surviving a challenge.** |
239:1. ***How We Learn to Move*** — the foundation, and still the best plain-language on-ramp for a clinician. **This is gap 2; buy this one first.**
240:2. ***Learning to Optimize Movement***
241:3. ***Learning To Be an "Ecological" Coach: Developing Attuned & Adaptable Coaching Skills*** — **note the real title; this file previously said "How to Be an Ecological Coach", which does not exist.**
248:**Recommendation:** take all eight free guides now; buy *How We Learn to Move*; **join the CLA certification waitlist only if Joe's development budget is real** — $1,995 buys direct feedback from the textbook's co-author, which nothing else in this file offers, but the free material plus the Emergence blog covers most of the same ground at zero cost.
259:**1. Gray's four-step coaching cycle, from his new book — the process model the phase-2 tool should support.**
297:**The two legitimate reasons to change a movement — and the instruction not to fix what isn't broken.** Gray is explicit that you change a solution for **performance or injury** — *"often those go hand in hand"* — and never because it looks unusual: **"if the player is doing the worst ugly swing you've ever seen but their bat speed is high, leave it alone. Don't change things unless there's a good reason."** **In a rehab setting, where "it looks wrong" drives a great deal of intervention, this is the most challenging sentence in the file.** It also names injury as a first-class reason to intervene — **the clinician's mandate, stated by the textbook's co-author.**
